body:
did you know the crystals on the showgirl covers were never actually made for taylor?

the feathered, rhinestoned looks across "the life of a showgirl" are vintage bob mackie -- the designer behind cher and decades of the las vegas stage. except mackie says nobody asked him. the pieces were borrowed from his old "jubilee!" revue, and by his account he found out the same way the rest of us did, calling himself "kind of shocked" to see her wearing them.

and the concept leans all the way in. taylor shot six different showgirl portraits with mert and marcus -- their first time photographing her since reputation's black-and-white newsprint era -- so the album is basically her as six different showgirls. yet the standard cover isn't full glam at all: it's her half-submerged in a bathtub, because, she said, her days on the eras tour "ended in a bathtub, not usually in a bedazzled dress." the glamour machine, shot from inside the dressing room instead of from the audience.

(and that likeness people keep clocking to millais's painting of ophelia? a fan-and-critic read -- she never confirmed it.)
